clue.text: Plot course of river?

definitions.meaning: a small patch of garden ground planted with blooms
read whimsically, a 'flower' is anything that flows, and a river's course is its bed

explanation.definitionFit: A garden plot for blooms is a planted bed, and a river (something that flows) runs along its bed, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Government department alters book prefaces

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department
to reword a text is to alter its wording

explanation.surface: A ministry tinkers with the introductory pages of an official book.
explanation.walkthrough: FO, the Foreign Office, is a UK government department.
explanation.definitionFit: Introductory pieces placed before the main text of a book are its prefatory sections, also called prefaces.

clue.text: The Undeveloped Seed Louvre rehung without right

indicators.note: pictures rehung in a gallery are rearranged, so the letters that remain are put in a new order
without says a letter is dropped from the gallery's name

explanation.surface: A painting with a book-like title is moved around the walls of the Paris gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes R from LOUVRE, leaving LOUVE, which 'rehung' rearranges. The italic 'The Undeveloped Seed' poses as an artwork's title; 'The' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany this is the structure in a plant's ovary that becomes a seed once fertilised.

clue.text: Flat ring provided for taking part in riding contest

parts.note: a flat surface is even
a ting is a light ringing sound

explanation.surface: A level arena with a ring is laid on for an equestrian competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat ring' looks like a horsey arena but gives two pieces; 'provided for' is only link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing in a horse trials event of dressage, cross-country and jumping is this equestrian sport.

clue.text: Cricket shot certain to go over a railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: bound to go means sure to do so

explanation.surface: A batsman's stroke is sure to fly across the railway line beside the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a shot reaching the edge of the field scores four or six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit that reaches the rope at the field's edge, scoring four or six runs, is named after that edge.

clue.text: It's a mistake to change sides

definitions.meaning: to desert one's country or party for the other side

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a fault or flaw, and the verb means to desert to the opposing camp.

clue.text: What witch may use to live thus —— magic, primarily

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word magic

explanation.surface: A witch's habits: living a certain way, by magic first of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom of twigs tied to a handle is what a witch traditionally rides.

clue.text: Ship — British one needing specialist engineers

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A British vessel is short of crew and needs a team of technical engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient galley with two banks of oars is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Omen: about superior English ruler

indicators.note: about means the word for omen goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an omen is a sign
over means above, superior in position

explanation.surface: A portent concerning a high-ranking English monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch, a king or queen holding supreme power, is a supreme ruler.

clue.text: Glum youth following second feeble-minded person

indicators.note: following puts the youth's name after the word for second

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
Ron Glum was the dim son in the old BBC radio comedy The Glums

explanation.surface: A gloomy teenager trails behind a dim-witted companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glum' looks like an adjective for a sulky boy, but it is a surname: Ron Glum was the dozy son in 'The Glums', a 1950s British radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid, dim-witted individual is called this as an insult.

clue.text: Gold on order, say, for a cylindrical pile of coins

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
say means the word for order is pronounced, giving a French-looking spelling

parts.note: a rule is an order or regulation
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A request for gold leads to a stack of coins wrapped in paper.
explanation.walkthrough: ROULE sounds like 'rule' (order), and AU, gold's chemical symbol, goes on after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of coins stacked and wrapped in paper is this French term.

clue.text: Warning cry very short as always.

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn of a ball in flight

indicators.note: short means the word very loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone forever shouts brief warnings.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golfer's shout to warn people of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting for all time, eternally, is the same as always.

clue.text: Question about introduction of Egyptian grain

indicators.note: about means the question word goes round the next letter

parts.note: what is a question word

indicators.note: introduction of points to the first letter of the word Egyptian

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the first Egyptian crop.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal crop, ground into flour, is a staple grain grown since ancient times along the Nile.

clue.text: What could make me read on, devouring 100 stories?

indicators.note: devouring means the rearranged letters take in another letter
asks what these words could be rearranged into, so their letters are mixed

parts.note: the anagram fodder
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A gripping collection of a hundred tales that keeps one turning the pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could make' rearranges ME READ ON to DEAMERON; 'devouring' puts C, Roman 100, inside. Boccaccio's work holds exactly 100 stories, so the clue is neatly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's fourteenth-century collection of a hundred tales told by ten young Florentines is a book of stories.

clue.text: This may clarify what's crude about showy dress

parts.note: re means about, concerning
finery is elaborate, showy clothing

explanation.surface: A remark about vulgar clothing explains what is coarse about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' suggests vulgarity, but it is crude oil, which a plant purifies.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial plant purifies crude oil or sugar, so it clarifies raw material.

clue.text: Definite last word on closure of pit? Heavens!

parts.note: firm means definite, fixed
amen is the last word of a prayer

indicators.note: closure of points to the last letter of the word pit

explanation.surface: A miner's exclamation on hearing the colliery will definitely shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation, but it is the definition, the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The vault of the sky, poetically, is the heavens.

clue.text: Indication of engaged status? Yes and no

definitions.text: Indication of engaged status? Yes and no

parts.words: Indication of engaged status? Yes and no
parts.note: a token on the finger shows a betrothal, yet the same sound from a telephone shows the line is free, not engaged

explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is marked by one on the finger, while a phone giving this tone is free rather than busy.

clue.text: Verdant upland turned over to make space for resting players

parts.note: verdant means green

indicators.note: turned means the word for upland is read backwards

parts.note: a moor is a stretch of open upland

explanation.surface: Grassy high ground is turned over to make an area where actors can relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses MOOR to ROOM. A theatre's green room is where performers wait offstage.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, the lounge where actors wait and relax when not on stage is so called.

clue.text: Ambassador wrong to imprison priest for seven days

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: to imprison means the word for wrong is put around the priest

parts.note: bad means wrong
Dom is a title given to some Catholic priests and monks

explanation.surface: An envoy is unjustly made to jail a clergyman for a week.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title; Dom is the title of Benedictine monks.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek for seven, it is a period of a week or any group of seven.

clue.text: Small book advocating limit restricting speed and end of driving-test

indicators.note: restricting means the word for limit encloses the speed unit

parts.note: a pale is a boundary, a limit
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of driving-test

explanation.surface: A leaflet urges a speed limit and the end of the driving test.
explanation.walkthrough: A pale is a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'. The definition includes 'advocating' because such a tract argues a case; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tract, often arguing for a cause, is a small booklet issued to persuade.

clue.text: Type that's abandoned Sally

indicators.note: abandoned means the letters for that is are dropped

parts.note: a sortie is a sally, a sudden attack out of a besieged place
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A kind of person who has left Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a sortie; 'that's' gives IE (id est, 'that is').
explanation.definitionFit: A kind or variety is a type.

clue.text: I'm imprisoned for first of debts — when due I needed 50% only

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of debts

parts.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival, says when someone is due

indicators.note: 50% only means just the first half of the word needed is kept

explanation.surface: A debtor laments being jailed after paying only half when the bill fell due.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in custody can say they are locked up, so the definition is a prisoner speaking.

clue.text: You'll see ball-game in covering winter sports venue

indicators.note: in means the ball game goes inside the covering

parts.note: skin is a covering
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Somewhere wrapped up warm you watch a ball game at a winter resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared slope for skiing is a venue for winter sports.

clue.text: False top right to be removed from cosy American home

parts.note: a wig is false hair on top of the head

indicators.note: to be removed from means a letter is taken out of the word for cosy

parts.note: warm means cosy

explanation.surface: A toupee must come off in a snug American house.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed dwelling of the Native peoples of North America is an American home.

clue.text: One of the king's half-baked songsters?

definitions.text: One of the king's half-baked songsters?

parts.words: One of the king's half-baked songsters?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence has four and twenty singing birds baked in a pie set before the king

explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, two dozen of these singing birds are baked in a pie for the king.

clue.text: *Some cable's specially wound

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A specially made cable has been coiled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like the past of 'wind' (the cable coiled), but it is the verb to injure: an obsolete sense, from French blesser.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic meaning, from French blesser, is to injure or hurt.

clue.text: Power line in that support structure?

definitions.text: Power line in that support structure?

parts.words: Power line in that support structure?
parts.note: a tall steel lattice tower holds overhead electricity cables, so the cable is in it

explanation.definitionFit: A tall steel tower carrying overhead electricity cables supports the power line.

clue.text: Drunk, on about two pints or less

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
re means about

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy is going on about drinking less than a couple of pints.
explanation.walkthrough: The metric unit holds about 1.76 pints, a little under two.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric measure of volume equals about one and three quarter pints.

clue.text: Part of face to look almost tanned

parts.note: to eye is to look at

indicators.note: almost means the word for tanned loses its last letter

parts.note: tanned skin is brown

explanation.surface: A beauty note: one feature looks nearly suntanned.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of hair above each eye is a feature of the face.

clue.text: Greek character's total transformation as half-caste

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: transformation means the letters of the word total are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek figure undergoes a complete change of identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person but is the letter mu. The answer is a dated term, now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated, now offensive term for a person with one Black and one white parent, of mixed race.

clue.text: Observed conference material

definitions.meaning: ..., as on a meeting, means attended it as an observer

explanation.definitionFit: To have sat in on a meeting is to have observed it, and the joined word is a glossy silk fabric.

clue.text: I'm taken aback by vision about holy man half-way across river

indicators.note: taken aback means the letters of I'm are read backwards
about means the word for vision goes round the holy man

parts.note: a dream is a vision
St, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: Someone is startled by a vision of a saint while fording a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of a stream, halfway across a river, is the phrase's literal sense.
